 Oral Judgment
1. The appellants/petitioners have challenged the quantum of compensation awarded in the Judgment and award dated 31.01.2020 passed in MVC No.474/2014 by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Chincholi.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel for the respondent No.3.
3.
Learned counsel for the appellants would contend that, the deceased was a cleaner and considering his avocation, the income taken at Rs.7,500/- by the tribunal is on lower side.

He submits that, even though the deceased was divorcee he died survived appellant No.1-mother and appellant No.2-minor daughter and therefore, the deductions taken by the tribunal at 50% is not proper and as against that, deductions to be taken at 1/3rd for personal expenses of the deceased.

He submits that, the appellant No.1/petitioner No.1 being the minor is entitled to filial compensation of Rs.40,000/- and appellant No.2/petitioner No.2 being the daughter of the deceased is entitled to parental consortium NC: 2025:KHC-K:4496 HC-KAR of Rs.40,000/-.
With this he prays to allow the appeal and enhance the compensation awarded by the tribunal.

4. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3 would contend that, the deceased was aged 37 years and the multiplier taken at '16' is not proper as per Sarla Verma case, and the proper multiplier applicable is '15'.
She further submits that, the deceased was a cleaner in the lorry and therefore, the income taken by the tribunal is proper and correct.
He further submits that, the future prospects taken at 50% is not proper as the deceased was self employed and therefore, the future prospects have to be taken at 40%.
With this she submits that, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is on higher side.
5. Having heard the learned counsels, this Court has perused the impugned Judgment and the trial Court records.
6. On perusal of the Postmortem Report and Inquest Mahazar, the age of the deceased noted in them is 37 years.
Therefore, there is no basis for the tribunal to take the age of the deceased between 31 to 35 years.

As the deceased NC: 2025:KHC-K:4496 HC-KAR was aged 37 years, the multiplier taken by the tribunal at '16' is not proper and the multiplier applicable is '15'.
7.
The deceased was a cleaner and the petitioners have not placed on record any proof of income of the deceased.
Considering the same, the tribunal has rightly taken notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,500/- per month.

sentences.text: The deceased even though was a divorcee, died survived the petitioner No.1-mother and petitioner No.2- minor daughter, who were dependent on him and therefore, the deduction towards personal expenses of the deceased has to be taken at 1/3rd instead of half i.e. 50% as taken by the tribunal.
9. The deceased was not having any permanent job and as he is aged below 40 years, the future prospects have to be taken as 40% as against 50% taken by the tribunal.

10. In view of the above, the loss of dependency is as follows:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4496 HC-KAR Rs.7,500/- + 40% (future prospects) = Rs.10,500/-
Rs.10,500/- X 12 X 15 X 2/3 = Rs.12,60,000/-.
11.
The deceased died survived his mother i.e. appellant No.1/petitioner No.1 and the minor daughter i.e. appellant No.2/petitioner No.2.

Therefore, the appellant No.1/petitioner No.1 is entitled to filial compensation of Rs.40,000/- and appellant No.2/petitioner No.2 is entitled to parental consortium of Rs.40,000/- as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130.
